title: Gyoza
subtitle: Japanese pan-fried pork and cabbage dumplings
excerpt: Crisp-bottomed, tender-topped Japanese dumplings filled with pork mince, cabbage, ginger, and garlic. Pan-fried and steamed in the same pan to produce the classic two-texture result.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gyoza are Japanese dumplings adapted from the Chinese jiaozi, brought to Japan by soldiers and settlers returning from Manchuria in the post-Second World War period. The Japanese adaptation is characterised by a thinner wrapper than the Chinese original, a more garlicky filling, and the distinctive cooking method: first pan-fried (to crisp the base), then steamed in the pan by adding water and immediately covering with a lid, then uncovered to crisp the base again. This produces the characteristic gyoza with a crisp golden base and a tender, steamed top. The filling is always well-seasoned and flavoured with garlic and ginger, which are more prominent in gyoza than in most Chinese dumpling fillings. Gyoza wrappers are available from Asian supermarkets; making them from scratch is possible but requires significant time.

recipeTools.notes: A large non-stick frying pan with a lid.

content.text: Squeeze the cabbage in a clean cloth after salting to remove as much water as possible. Excess moisture in the filling makes the dumplings soggy and stops the base from crisping. The pan-fry, steam, and crisp method needs a little confidence: add the water and lid quickly after the first fry to trap the steam, then remove the lid and let the water boil off fully to crisp the base again. Serve at once. Gyoza deteriorate quickly and should not be left sitting.

items.preparation: for the wrappers, or use 40 ready-made gyoza wrappers from an Asian supermarket
very finely shredded, salted, squeezed dry

content.text: Combine the pork mince, squeezed cabbage, garlic, ginger, spring onion, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a bowl. Mix thoroughly. Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper. Dampen the edge of the wrapper with water and fold to a half-moon, pleating the edge with small folds to seal.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the gyoza flat-side down in rows without touching. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the bases are golden-brown.

Add 100 ml of water to the pan and immediately cover with a lid. Steam for 4 minutes until the water has evaporated. Remove the lid and continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes to re-crisp the bases. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce (soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, and sliced chilli stirred together).
